column1: # AQL Language Specification: convert <Ideal> to Map / List
# Every Ideal value can be converted to a Map or a List via
# `convert Map <ideal>` / `convert List <ideal>`. The conversion is a
# per-type capability (IdealConverter); the base Ideal — and thus the
# fallback for any Ideal that does not override it, including user-defined
# Ideals — yields an empty Map ({}) or empty List ([]).
# §1  a user-defined Ideal (refine Object …) falls back to {} / []
def Foo (refine Object {x:Integer}) convert Map (make Foo {x:5})
def Foo (refine Object {x:Integer}) convert List (make Foo {x:5})
def Foo (refine Object {x:Integer}) typeof (convert Map (make Foo {x:5}))
def Foo (refine Object {x:Integer}) typeof (convert List (make Foo {x:5}))
# §2  a bare nominal Ideal subtype also falls back
def Bar (refine Object {}) convert Map (make Bar {})
def Bar (refine Object {}) convert List (make Bar {})
# §3  negative — an Ideal converts only to Map or List
def Foo (refine Object {}) convert Integer (make Foo {})
